subject: Request: Subprocessor key handback and data export evidence
messages:
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@clinxhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor key handback and proof of export

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our security team reviewed Redwood's SIG answers and had two follow-ups before we sign off on production access: 1) we need a clear plan for KMS key handback / escrow in the event Redwood terminates a subprocessor or moves keys between providers, and 2) an auditable manifest showing the exact files/records exported for onboarding customers (we want to validate a sample export).

Specifically, can you provide:
- Your subprocessor roster with the crypto responsibilities column filled (who holds keys vs who has wrapped/encrypted data).
- A short sequence diagram or PDF that shows how an ephemeral provider key is rotated/returned and who retains custody.
- An example export manifest (schema + sample entries) for one recent onboarding export.

We'd like to include that in our SOC2 scope and surface it in procurement. If possible, can you share something by Monday 6/14? If there are steps that need internal approvals we'll understand — just want to set expectations.

Thanks,
Sanjay Mehta
Head of Infrastructure Security
ClinX Health

--
Sanjay Mehta
ClinX Health

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@clinxhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor key handback and proof of export

Hi Sanjay —

Appreciate the clear ask. We can provide the artifacts you describe. Quick overview of what we'll deliver and timing:

1) Subprocessor roster (crypto responsibilities) — spreadsheet with columns for provider, role, crypto custody, residency, SLA for key handback. We will mark any onshore-only providers and note where Redwood acts as key custodian vs provider-managed keys.

2) KMS/key handback flow — a 1-page diagram (PDF) plus a short narrative describing handback triggers: contract termination, subprocessor removal, and emergency key rotation. This will include the cryptographic wrapping steps and the audit trail we generate.

3) Export manifest sample — JSON manifest (schema + 3 sample rows) and a verification checklist we use when fulfilling a data export request.

I'll attach drafts and loop in our Infrastructure Security lead, Ben, who can confirm the key control language. Marissa, can you confirm we can include the export manifest sample from the Q2 onboarding run? It contains redacted PII, but we can redact and provide an example.

We can get a bundle to you by Monday. If you need an attest-style cover note for procurement (e.g., "evidence provided represents production procedures as of 2027-06-01"), Ben and I can sign off.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: (to follow)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor key handback and proof of export

Grace, Ben — quick note from the ops side: we can produce a redacted export manifest from the June 3 onboarding job. I recommend the following redactions: remove customer identifiers, replace GUIDs with sample-IDs, and truncate any large blob references. The manifest schema is stable (fields: export_id, customer_id_redacted, export_ts, object_type, file_ref, sha256).

Ben: can you confirm that the KMS handback process we documented in the "key-escrow playbook" covers the two scenarios Sanjay mentions (termination + emergency rotation)? If yes, I'll pull the diagram from the repo and produce the PDF.

Will target noon PT Monday for the bundle.

-Marissa
Director, Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@clinxhealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 11:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor key handback and proof of export

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks for the ask. Attached is the evidence bundle you requested: 1) redwood_subprocessor_roster_v2.xlsx (crypto roles populated), 2) kms_keyflow_diagram.pdf (1-page sequence diagram + narrative), and 3) data_export_manifest.json (schema + redacted sample rows). A few implementation notes below:

- Key custody: Redwood uses a split-custody model for hosted keys — cloud KMS for encryption-at-rest plus a wrapped-ephemeral key held by the subprocessor when they need transform access. The roster marks providers that have direct KMS access vs wrapped-key operations.
- Handback triggers: contract termination (30-day notice by default with expedited 72-hour handback for high-risk providers), confirmed breach, or explicit key rotation request from customer. Handback steps: revoke subprocessor KMS IAM, export wrapped key material to customer-designated escrow (if requested), rotate wrapping key, and record the operation in an immutable audit log (link included).
- Evidence: the KMS diagram includes the audit log sample IDs; the export manifest is a redacted sample and includes a hash we can surface for validation.

Links of interest: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleLinkToEvidence

If you want a formal cover letter signed for procurement, say the word and we'll add it (we typically include a one-paragraph attestation and the bundle).

Best,
Ben Carter
Infrastructure Security Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_roster_v2.xlsx, kms_keyflow_diagram.pdf, data_export_manifest.json
